name: Varnish & Craquelure
desc: The conservation-lab pass: the frame goes under aged amber varnish with an uneven drifting film that both dims the picture and scatters its own plate tone back out, foxing spots bloom and catch the room, canvas weave tooth breaks the surface, a craquelure net opens across it, and a gallery lamp wanders the gloss so the raised crack lips ignite wherever it rakes.

energy.doc: strength of everything the panel emits — plate tone, blooms, the lamp and the sheen

scale.doc: size of the weave pitch, the craquelure cells, the blooms and the lamp

glaze.doc: how heavy the aged varnish film is — both how much it dims the picture and how much plate tone it scatters back

craze.doc: how far the craquelure net has opened, and how hard its lips catch the lamp

density.doc: number of varnish blooms and foxing spots

speed.doc: how fast the lamp and the film drift

x.doc: centre the lamp wanders about, x

y.doc: centre the lamp wanders about, y (also the foxed tide-line height)

style.doc: varnish: aged amber film on canvas, cracked and lit · foxed: paper gone mouldy, brown spots and a water tide-line · wet: fresh varnish just brushed on — saturated, glossy, uncracked · xray: the conservator's radiograph — desaturated, the crack net wide open

act.doc: gallery: a lamp wandering the gloss · raking: the conservator's lamp sweeps hard across the surface · age: the varnish yellows and the crack net opens over minutes

seed.doc: deterministic seed — weave, crack net, foxing and bloom placement
